entries_new.name: Free City of Danzig (1807 to 1814)
entries_new.stopped_by: Russian and Prussian occupation (January 1814) and return to the King of Prussia (19 February 1814)
entries_new.challenge: Russian and Prussian forces occupied the city on 2 January 1814
entries_new.mechanism: A treaty between France and Prussia made the city and its surrounding territory independent under the protection of two kings.
entries_new.story:
Danzig, now Gdańsk in Poland, was made a free city by a treaty signed at Tilsit on 9 July 1807 by France and Prussia, which took effect on 12 July 1807. The treaty restored the city and its surrounding territory to independence under the protection of the kings of Prussia and Saxony.
Russian and Prussian forces occupied the city on 2 January 1814, and on 3 February a Prussian-appointed military governor took over its administration. At a ceremony on 19 February 1814 possession was returned to the King of Prussia, and the Congress of Vienna confirmed this on 9 June 1815. The source does not describe the city's internal government in these years.

entries_new.name: Portuguese India (Estado da Índia)
entries_new.founder: Kingdom of Portugal; Afonso de Albuquerque
entries_new.challenge: India annexed the territories in December 1961
entries_new.recognition: Portugal recognised Indian sovereignty over Goa, Daman and Diu in 1974
entries_new.mechanism: Portugal ruled coastal footholds in India through viceroys and governors-general sent from Lisbon.
entries_new.story:
Portuguese India, the Estado da Índia, was Portugal's government of its territories in India. A Portuguese fleet first landed at Calicut on 20 May 1498. In 1510 admiral Afonso de Albuquerque defeated the Bijapur sultans on behalf of a local ruler, Timayya, and a permanent settlement followed at Old Goa. Cochin served as capital until 1530, and later Nova Goa. Francisco de Almeida was the first viceroy (1505 to 1509).
By the 20th century the territory was Goa, the coastal enclaves of Daman and Diu, and the inland enclaves of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, acquired in 1779. India annexed the territories in December 1961; the source gives 19 December 1961, though its own table lists Goa to 1962. After the Carnation Revolution of 1974, Portugal restored relations with India and recognised Indian sovereignty.

entries_new.name: John Brown's Provisional Constitution and the Harpers Ferry raid
aka: Provisional Constitution and Ordinances for the People of the United States
entries_new.stopped_by: Virginia militia and US Marines under Colonel Robert E. Lee, 17 to 18 October 1859
entries_new.pop: 21 followers at the start of the raid
entries_new.laws: A 48-article Provisional Constitution adopted at Chatham, Canada, in May 1858
entries_new.challenge: Militia and US Marines; Brown was convicted of murder, treason and inciting a slave insurrection
entries_new.mechanism: A written constitution was adopted to govern an armed group during a planned war against slavery, and the group seized a federal arsenal.
entries_new.story:
In May 1858 the abolitionist John Brown held a convention at Chatham, Canada, attended by nearly four dozen men, more than thirty of them Black. The delegates adopted his Provisional Constitution and Ordinances for the People of the United States, a 48-article document meant to govern the group during a war to end slavery, and elected officers.
On 16 October 1859 Brown led 18 of his 21 followers into Harpers Ferry, Virginia, where the federal arsenal held about 100,000 weapons. Militia cut off their escape on 17 October, and on 18 October US Marines under Colonel Robert E. Lee stormed the engine house and captured Brown. He was convicted on 2 November 1859 of murder, treason and inciting a slave insurrection, and hanged on 2 December 1859.
